retakes.line: Attention. In simple terms, it's just the model deciding, for every word it's about to write, how much to focus on each word you give it.

retakes.line: So quick recap. Attention is the model deciding how much to focus on each part of what you said, by matching each word's query against every other word's key.
The encoder builds a picture of what your message is. The decoder writes the reply while constantly glancing back at it.
retakes.note: Delivery 1 runs off the rails mid-way ('...while constantly, while constantly, the encoder builds a picture of what your message') and is restarted. The pinned Whisper fixture shows none of that; it reads as one clean pair of sentences over 606.32-633.78.

protected.note: The video's own hook — 'Have you ever given an AI three things to do in one message? ... and it does the first two and just skips the third?' Said once. Named because B-238's equivalent on C038 was proposed for deletion.

'Every other word turns itself into a kind of answer key, advertising what it's about.' This is the OTHER half of a deliberate parallel construction, and D-365's one known false positive pairs it with 'Every word turns itself into a question' (real_transcripts.rs::the_one_measured_false_positive_is_this_one, pair 30/32). It is unique content and must never be cut.

'It's less — it's less read than write, and more read than write while constantly rechecking.' ONE sentence with a two-word stutter, not two deliveries: nothing here is said twice. B-246's C040 case proposes cutting 430.52-434.36 of it (proposed_cuts.rs, parakeet #36, 3.84 s).

unlabelled_rationale: Everything inside labelled_span that is not a delivery and not neutral is unique content: speech that exists nowhere else in this source, so proposing it for deletion is over-cutting. Known repeats deliberately NOT labelled as deliveries, because the repeated material is a sub-segment fragment in every reading and a whole-utterance take cannot express it without taking unique speech with it (see README, 'expressibility'): 'for watching / for watching' at ~681 s (two words), the 'A few months later' class of one-word mid-sentence corrections, and 'Jevons paradox' style emphatic repetition.
